messages:
olivia: Heads-up: I'm prototyping a 'lazy bisection' warmup for huge sharded safetensors. Idea is to progressively hydrate only the minimal byte ranges needed for the current KV access pattern using a binary-split heuristic, then expand as generation demands more layers/keys. Reduce first-token latency without prefetching whole shards.

samir: can you sketch the bisection heuristic? is it per-layer, per-tensor, or per-shard?

olivia: per-shard, but with a layer-awareness hint. Start with a tiny head-range (first X MB), if eviction hits or KV-miss for requested address, split that range in half and fetch the half containing the address. Repeat until the tensor region is present. We bind checksums to ranges so partial verification is possible.

jia: interesting. How do we handle safetensors metadata? safetensors assumes contiguous arrays, so ranges might cut across array boundaries.

olivia: yes — we add a tiny RangeIndex sidecar in the bundle: list of (tensor_name, byte_start, byte_end, range_checksum). If a fetch range slices a tensor, runtime reads minimal header then issues a follow-up to fetch remaining contiguous bytes for that tensor. We try to avoid many small fetches by aligning initial splits to tensor-aligned boundaries when we can.

rahul: what about atomicity? we can't expose partially verified weights. If a range fetch fails mid-stream we need rollback and fallback to manifest-full fetch.

olivia: agreed. Plan: ranges are fetched into a staging buffer + checksum-verified. Only after verification we commit into the shared cache. If verify fails we mark range bad and schedule fallback to manifest-based stream (full-shard read) and emit telemetry event: weight.onboard.failure.range_checksum.

samir: latency-wise, sounds good. But network load could spike with many small bisections across many requests. Any backpressure/aggregation plan?

olivia: yes — the warmup coordinator will coalesce concurrent overlapping range requests, and we have a cheap range-priority queue: hottest ranges (prefix-heavy) get larger initial seeds. Also adaptive backoff: after N splits in M ms, escalate to prefetch the remaining shard.

jia: also need compatibility with existing manifestless bundles and gzip/chunked transports. If compressed, range indexing must reference compressed offsets or we can't do partial reads.

olivia: thought about that — for compressed artifacts we only support whole-chunk addressing (chunk granularity). RangeIndex contains either raw offsets or chunk-IDs depending on compression. For gzip we currently fallback to chunk-granularity bisection (coarser but safe).

rahul: rollout strategy? this is risky for customers with strict determinism needs.

olivia: feature-flagged behind runtime rollout and only enabled for models opted-in via model manifest: "onboard_strategy: lazy_bisection". Default remains index-first or full-shard hotstart. Also add canary on a small pool with telemetry guard-rails: token latency, failure rate, checksum_mismatch_rate.

samir: any proto/cost for adding RangeIndex to existing safetensors packs? migration path?

olivia: RangeIndex is an optional sidecar: file.safetensors.rangeindex.json. We provide an indexer tool that scans existing safetensors and emits the sidecar. For registry-hosted bundles we'll auto-generate sidecars on upload. Older bundles without sidecars use conservative hotstart.

jira-style snippet (pseudocode):
```
function fetch_byte(addr):
  range = find_cached_range(addr)
  if range: return read_cached(addr)
  seed = initial_seed_for(range)
  fetch(seed)
  while not contains(addr):
    (left,right) = bisect(seed)
    fetch(right if addr in right else left)
    verify_and_commit()
    if failures > threshold: fallback_full_shard()
  return read_cached(addr)
```

ops-bot: deploy-note: flag "lazy-bisection" set to off globally. Enable only in canary/eng-ml-nonprod.

rahul: QA checklist suggestions: deterministic seeding tests, bad-range injection tests (checksum mismatch), concurrency storm sim, and cache-eviction interplay tests.

olivia: noted — I'll open a short RFC follow-up with prototyping notes, RangeIndex spec, metrics list, and a small perf benchmark plan. Thanks all. :rocket:
